front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《17》

en: Watching the reeds along the riverbank
How to stir the flowing light's reflection
How to recall the hazy years
Having crossed the Chu River, I am but a foot soldier
Songs of Chu rise on every side, each note urging on
And you, still watching the chess game without a word?

points.zh: 象棋的楚河界線中，常有二句警言 : 「起手無回大丈夫，棋中不語真君子」。
points.en: Along the "Chu River" dividing line in Chinese chess, there are two commonly cited maxims: "A true man does not take back a move once made; a true gentleman does not talk while playing."

en: Give him the starry sky, and give him imagination too
Give him a fishing rod
Also gave him "The Old Man and the Sea"

points.zh: 《老人與海》是海明威創作生涯的代表作品，是世界小說創作的經典。海明威於1954獲得諾貝爾文學獎。《老人與海》的主題和梅爾維爾的《白鯨記》類似， 都是描寫人類和大自然的博鬥和奮爭。《白鯨記》記述亞赫船長一心一意追殺大白鯨的故事， 因其違反自然規律，獨斷獨行，甚至祭出人性，用生命做籌碼跟命運下賭注，最終賠上生命，被大海吞噬。反之，《老人與海》的老船夫，在與大自然博鬥時，能心神沉穩，順天應時。在發揮堅忍， 勇氣，信心和決心等崇高人性的同時，体會萬物生存和并存之道，從而與大自然的本質和運行合而為一。《老人與海》提示了人生境界，也對生命各層面有提醒的象徵意義。
points.en: "The Old Man and the Sea" is the representative work of Hemingway's writing career and a classic of world fiction. Hemingway won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954. The theme of "The Old Man and the Sea" is similar to that of Melville's "Moby-Dick": both depict the struggle and striving between man and nature. "Moby-Dick" tells the story of Captain Ahab, who single-mindedly pursues and hunts the great white whale; because this violates the laws of nature, and because of his arbitrary, self-willed obsession—even wagering his life and his very humanity against fate—he ultimately pays with his life, swallowed by the sea. In contrast, the old fisherman of "The Old Man and the Sea," while struggling against nature, remains calm and steady in spirit, following the way of heaven and the seasons. While displaying such noble human qualities as perseverance, courage, faith, and determination, he comes to understand the way in which all things live and coexist, and thereby becomes one with the essential nature and the workings of the natural world. "The Old Man and the Sea" points toward a certain state of human existence, and carries symbolic meaning that reminds us of the many dimensions of life.

en: Let win and loss fade into the distance
At the hour of sunset
Watching the reeds sway in the wind
The evening wind gently blows
The color of the grass faint and low, once
At life's turning point, I once waited for you

zh: 而我，紅塵已遠，紛繁不再
en: Lao Tzu said, the five colors blind the eye
And I, the dust of the world now far, the tangle no more
Now, only a single color remains to long for

points.zh:
老子《 道德經 》第十二章:
五色令人目盲，五音令人耳聾，五味令人口爽。馳騁畋獵，令人心發狂，難得之貨，令人行妨。
points.en:
Laozi, Tao Te Ching, Chapter 12:
The five colors blind the eye; the five tones deafen the ear; the five flavors dull the palate. Racing and hunting madden the mind; goods that are hard to obtain lead one's conduct astray.

en: At that time we sat in silence
Facing the fallen leaves
Distracted
Mist and clouds for a thousand miles, and now
No longer counting, who is it
Who was exiled, and who regretted whom?
Releasing a white dove, releasing a bluebird
Flying once more with the wind
Pursuing a distant dream

zh: 偶而一時恍惚， 就浮出
en: Now and then, in a moment's daze, it surfaces
A summer shower over the Chianan Plain
Egret white, rice-ear yellow, banana green

points.zh:
《 美麗島》   節錄
詩 / 詞 :  陳秀喜，梁景峰    作曲 : 李雙澤
我們搖籃的美麗島
是母親溫暖的懷抱
驕傲的祖先們正視著
正視著我們的腳步 
他們一再重覆的叮嚀
不要忘記，不要忘記 
婆娑無邊的太平洋
懷抱著自由的土地
我們這裡有勇敢的人民
篳路藍縷，以啟山林 
我們這裡有無窮的生命
水牛，稻米，香蕉，玉蘭花
陳秀喜（1921-1991，台灣新竹人，長年居住嘉義關仔嶺，住家「笠園」）素有「台灣奇女子」、「台灣第一位女詩人」以及「台灣女性主義詩人的先驅」之譽。1970年代是台灣青年詩社崛起的年代，陳秀喜在1971年出版第一部中文詩集《覆葉》後，活躍新詩詩壇，擔任笠詩社社長20年（1971-1991）期間，是《笠》詩刊茁壯與活躍期，也是台灣意識與民主及社會運動的蓬勃期。1977年的鄉土文學論戰發生，陳秀喜於1973年寫的〈台灣〉一詩，經梁景峰教授改編歌詞，標題更換為《美麗島》，李雙澤作曲，民歌手胡德夫，楊袓珺等人演唱，風靡校園，傳唱全島。該詩詞語句貼切台灣，筆觸溫和委婉，表露台灣人的心聲。戒嚴時期曾遭禁唱，長達八年。她以女性潤滑劑的活躍者，溫柔仁愛的詩風，及長輩風範，贏得詩壇共同的愛戴。她的詩飽含關愛與充滿希望，她的詩愛與風範一直在島嶼傳唱著。    ( 民報，2015-09-02 )
2016年5月20日，總統就職典禮時，在蔡英文就職演說後，接著由國立實驗合唱團和敦化國小合唱團，帶動全場會衆一起合唱這首《美麗島》。
points.en:
"Formosa (Beautiful Island)" (excerpt)
Poem/Lyrics: Chen Hsiu-hsi, Liang Ching-feng; Music: Li Shuang-tse
This beautiful island, our cradle,
is our mother's warm embrace
Our proud ancestors watch closely,
watching closely over our footsteps
Again and again they repeat their reminder:
do not forget, do not forget
The boundless, swaying Pacific Ocean
embraces this land of freedom
Here we have a brave people
who, through hardship, opened up the mountains and forests
Here we have boundless life --
water buffalo, rice, bananas, and magnolia blossoms
Chen Hsiu-hsi (1921-1991), a native of Hsinchu, Taiwan, who lived for many years in Guanziling, Chiayi, in a home called "Li Yuan," was known as "Taiwan's remarkable woman," "Taiwan's first female poet," and "a pioneer of Taiwanese feminist poetry." The 1970s were a period when young poetry societies rose up in Taiwan. After publishing her first Chinese-language poetry collection, "Overturned Leaves," in 1971, Chen Hsiu-hsi became active in the modern poetry scene and served as president of the Li Poetry Society for twenty years (1971-1991), a period during which the Li poetry journal grew and flourished, and one that also coincided with a flourishing of Taiwanese consciousness, democracy, and social movements. After the 1977 Nativist Literature Debate, Chen Hsiu-hsi's 1973 poem "Taiwan" was adapted by Professor Liang Ching-feng, retitled "Formosa," and set to music by Li Shuang-tse; folk singers such as Hu Te-fu and Yang Tsu-chun performed it, and it swept through campuses and was sung across the entire island. The poem's language fits Taiwan closely, its tone gentle and understated, expressing the feelings of the Taiwanese people. It was banned from performance during martial law for as long as eight years. Through her role as an active and gentle presence among poets, her tender and compassionate poetic style, and her example as an elder, Chen Hsiu-hsi won the shared affection of the poetry world. Her poems are full of care and hope, and her poetic spirit continues to be sung across the island. (Min Pao, September 2, 2015)
On May 20, 2016, at the presidential inauguration ceremony, following President Tsai Ing-wen's inaugural address, the National Experimental Chorus and the Dunhua Elementary School Chorus led the entire audience in singing this song, "Formosa," together.
